panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Real infant clinical photograph showing marked generalized lichenification with erythroderma, hyperpigmentation, and accentuation of skin markings, explicitly attributed to atopic dermatitis. B: Close-up of an infant's arm and hand with severe lichenified, erythematous, hyperpigmented skin and accentuated markings in atopic dermatitis. C: Real infant clinical photograph with extensive erythroderma and well-demarcated shallow ulcerative eczematous lesions identified in the caption as eczema coxsackium, attributed to infantile atopic dermatitis.

plate_findings.evidence: Caption: “eczematous plaques of eczema in both extensors and flexors”

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Caption identifies this as a childhood atopic dermatitis phenotype and explicitly describes marked facial hyperpigmentation with hyperaccentuated skin markings and limited central facial sparing. B: Caption directly attributes the leg findings, including lichenification, to clinical aspects of childhood atopic dermatitis. C: Caption describes eczematous plaques involving both extensor and flexor surfaces with crusting in an older child with atopic dermatitis.

panels.figure_caption: Clinical aspects of atopic dermatitis in childhood. Panel (A) shows marked hyperpigmentation of the face and hyper accentuation of skin markings with sparing of the central face. This patient does not fully typify the central facial sparing as the sparing is limited to the nose. Panel (B) shows lichenification, in addition to hyperpigmentation and dryness of the legs. Panel (C) shows eczematous plaques of eczema in both extensors and flexors with superimposed crusting in an older child.

The linear distribution of the rash on the background of generalized AD, the histological findings and the pruritic nature of the rash also suggested superimposed Type 2 segmental AD. Improvement was noted after the use of topical corticosteroids, pimecrolimus cream 1% and emollients.
